resources.string: Set to true to allow the user to load a local HTML file into the WebView.\n\nThis will be accessible using the 3-dot icon on the right of the address bar.

The URL that can be returned to by:
 1. tapping the screen 10 times in quick succession
 2. using the floating toolbar icon
 3. using the address bar menu

This is also controlled by the "Allow Go Home" setting under web browsing.

Set to true to support PDF Rendering using Mozilla's PDF.js renderer:

- https://github.com/mozilla/pdf.js

You will first need to download the renderer by opening the popup menu for this
setting and clicking the "Download PDF.js assets" button.

---

PDF.js assets and PDF source requests are routed through
%1$s and handled locally by the app using the
WebViewAssetLoader API.

For more details, see:

https://developer.android.com/reference/androidx/webkit/WebViewAssetLoader
PDF rendering cannot be used until PDF.js assets are downloaded.

Specify regular expressions (regex), one per line.

Escaping with backslash (\) is required for special characters
in regex like '.' and '?'.

These patterns also use partial matching.
If you need strict control, anchor your regex with `^` and `$`.

Whitelist patterns take precedence over blacklist patterns.
Some lines contain invalid regular expressions.

Specify bookmarked URLs one per line. Blank lines will be ignored.

This is accessible in the address bar. See the relevant setting "Web Browsing -> Allow Bookmark Access".

You can also specify a title for display in the format: "<URL> | <Title>".

For example:

```

%1$s | Webview Kiosk

https://duckduckgo.com | DuckDuckGo

https://f-droid.org | F-Droid

```

Number of seconds of inactivity before the screen is dimmed.

This will set the brightness to 0, and will restore the brightness to
your device -> brightness setting upon new user interactions.

Minimum: %1$d

To disable, use the value 0.

When enabled, the app will immediately enter locked/pinned mode on startup,
preventing exit until unpinned.

On some devices, you may still be prompted with a confirmation screen.

Interval in seconds between automatic refresh attempts when a page fails
to load. This usually indicate the inability to connect to the server,
e.g. due to no internet connection or the server is offline.

Minimum: %1$d

To disable, use the value 0.

Select when the page should automatically refresh when network
connectivity is restored.

- Always: refresh whenever a network connection is available
- On Page Error: only refresh if the previous page load failed
- Never: do not refresh automatically

Number of seconds of inactivity before the app resets to the home URL.

When there is 5 seconds left, a warning countdown will be shown on
the screen.

User interactions the screen will reset the timer.

The navigation history will be cleared when resetting.

Minimum: %1$d

To disable, use the value 0.

When enabled, the app will always start fresh at the Home URL when
closed and re-opened, as opposed to the last visited URL.

The navigation history will also be cleared.
